research_notes_other.additional_notes: The Wrong Carlos: Anatomy of a Wrongful Execution represents one of the most comprehensive investigations into a potential wrongful execution ever conducted. The book is the result of a six-year investigation by Columbia Law School professor James Liebman and his students, who meticulously documented the case of Carlos DeLuna. The investigation compiled an extraordinary collection of primary documents and evidence...

media_item.item_title: Book Content: The Wrong Carlos: Anatomy of a Wrongful Execution
media_item.focus_or_theme: Wrongful execution, criminal justice system failures, death penalty critique, mistaken identity
media_item.summary_notes: This book details a six-year investigation into the wrongful execution of Carlos DeLuna.  It presents a meticulous compilation of evidence, including police and court files, crime scene photos, audiotapes, and witness interviews, to argue DeLuna's innocence. The book serves as both a case study and a critique of the US death penalty system, highlighting how systemic failures can lead to irreversible injustice.
media_item.case_details_raw: On February 4, 1983, Wanda Lopez was stabbed to death.  Carlos DeLuna was arrested 40 minutes later, and identified by a single eyewitness. No physical evidence linked DeLuna to the crime. DeLuna claimed another man, Carlos Hernandez, committed the murder.  The Columbia DeLuna Project's investigation revealed Hernandez's existence and history of similar crimes, a suppressed police audiotape showing a different suspect, and Hernandez's boasts of committing the murder.  Despite mounting evidence, DeLuna was executed on December 7, 1989.
key_quotes_raw: "No one cared enough about the defendant or the victim to make sure they caught the right guy." - James Liebman
"Everything that could go wrong in a death penalty case did go wrong for DeLuna." - James Liebman

"The very same factors that sent DeLuna to his death—faulty eyewitness testimony, shoddy legal representation, and prosecutorial misfeasance—continue to put innocent people at risk of execution today." - James Liebman
"Sadly, DeLuna's story is not unique." - James Liebman
"An infuriating yet engrossing book on wrongful conviction... An extraordinary and necessary book." - Publisher's description
systemic_issues_raw: Unreliability of eyewitness identification, particularly cross-ethnic identifications
Prosecutorial misconduct, including suppression of exculpatory evidence
Inadequate legal representation for indigent defendants
Failure of courts to properly review evidence of innocence
Racial and socioeconomic bias in the criminal justice system
Finality of the death penalty, which prevents correction of wrongful convictions
Lack of accountability for prosecutors and police who contribute to wrongful convictions
Systemic pressures to solve high-profile cases quickly
Failure to properly preserve and test forensic evidence
policy_recommendations_raw: Increased funding for public defenders and court-appointed attorneys
Videotaping of police investigations and interrogations
Improved preservation of crime scene evidence
More rigorous standards for admissibility of forensic evidence
Enhanced review procedures for capital cases
Reforms to allow for consideration of new evidence of innocence
Accountability measures for prosecutors who engage in misconduct
Abolition or moratorium on the death penalty
